objective.description: What the plan should optimise. **Use as few panels as possible**: cut every part, using the fewest panels; panels are used in the order listed. **Best use of the panels I have**: the panels can't fit every part, so choose which parts to cut to get the most out of them (by part value — see *Value*). **Shortest length from one panel**: you have one panel of fixed width and any length you need (e.g. a long board or a roll); cut every part using the shortest possible length. **Shortest width from one panel**: the same, but the length is fixed and the width is minimised.
objective.title: Goal
objective.x-short-help: The plan's aim: fewest panels, most from your panels, or shortest length or width.

panels.description: The stock panels to cut from, in the order they should be used.

The body of `POST /jobs`: what to solve, and for how long.

Only used for the OpenAPI description: the server reads the body field by field, to report every problem at once (see `request.rs`).

ended_by.description: Why the job ended: `complete` (the search ran to its end; a longer time limit would give the same plan), `time_limit` (a longer search may find a better plan) or `cancelled`. `null` until the job ends, and for a failed job.

Length.description: A length in millimetres, with at most one decimal (720, 3.2). More decimals are rejected, never rounded.

leftover_area.description: Area of the reusable leftover of the last panel.

panel_area.description: Total area of the panels used.

children.description: The rectangles this piece is cut into, side by side in the direction of the next stage's cuts. Empty for everything but pieces.

A rectangle in the cutting tree: the panel itself, an intermediate piece, or a final part, offcut or leftover.

id.description: Your name for this panel, shown on the cutting plan (e.g. "Birch ply 18 mm").
id.title: Name
id.x-short-help: Your name for this panel size, shown on the cutting plan.

length.description: The panel's long side, as delivered, in millimetres. For a panel with grain, the side along the grain. For "Shortest length from one panel", this is the maximum length available.
length.title: Length
length.x-short-help: The panel's long side in millimetres, along the grain if it has one.

quantity.description: How many panels of this size you have. Leave empty for "as many as needed".
quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.x-short-help: How many panels of this size you have; empty means as many as needed.

trims.description: Strips to cut off the panel's edges, named as the panel is drawn on the plan: the left and right ends, and the bottom and top long edges. Each edge has its *Trim* width and its *Trimmed strip*: how the strip is cut away. Leave them empty for clean factory edges.
trims.title: Trims
trims.x-short-help: Strips to cut off damaged panel edges before any part is placed.

width.description: The panel's short side, as delivered, in millimetres. For "Shortest width from one panel", this is the maximum width available.
width.title: Width
width.x-short-help: The panel's short side in millimetres.

grain.description: Tick if the part must keep the panel's grain direction (veneer, solid wood, wood-look melamine); it is then never turned. Leave unticked for MDF or chipboard: turning parts saves material.
grain.title: Keep grain direction
grain.x-short-help: Tick for veneer, solid wood or wood-look panels: the part is then never turned.

id.description: Your name for this part, shown on the cutting plan and labels (e.g. "Side left").
id.title: Name
id.x-short-help: Your name for this part, shown on the cutting plan.

length.title: Length

quantity.description: How many identical parts you need. With "Best use of the panels I have", this is the most that will be cut; fewer may be cut if they don't fit.
quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.x-short-help: How many identical parts you need.

value.description: Only used with "Best use of the panels I have": how much you want this part, compared with the others. The plan maximises the total value of the parts it cuts. Leave empty to value parts by their area in mm² (the plan then uses as much of the panel as possible). Set every part to 1 to cut as many parts as possible.
value.title: Value
value.x-short-help: How much you want this part when not every part fits; empty means its area.

width.description: The part's finished width in millimetres, before edge banding.
width.title: Width
width.x-short-help: The part's finished width in millimetres.

Pattern.description: One way of cutting a panel, possibly repeated on several identical panels.

first_cuts.description: The direction of the first, full-panel cuts.

panel_id.description: The name of the panel this pattern cuts.

repeat.description: How many panels are cut exactly this way.

root.description: The whole panel: the root of the cutting tree, at stage 0.

PlanReport.description: A plan found by a job, with its figures.

found_after.description: Seconds after the job started running when this plan was found.

metrics.description: Figures for this plan, computed by the independent checker.

number.description: 1 for the first plan found, 2 for the next better one, and so on.

plan.description: The cutting plan: one cutting tree per distinct way of cutting a panel.

cut_type.description: Whether a part may be cut free from a small offcut after the last stage. **Allowed** (recommended): a strip may hold parts of different sizes; a final trimming cut separates each part from its offcut. **Not allowed**: at the last stage every part must fill its strip exactly, with no offcut — fewer cuts, more waste. **One part per strip**: every part in a last-stage strip is the same part — the simplest plans to cut, the most waste.
cut_type.title: Last-stage trimming
cut_type.x-short-help: Whether a part may be trimmed free from a small offcut after the last stage.

first_cuts.description: Which way the first, full-panel cuts run. **Either** (recommended): the solver tries both and keeps the better plan. With one panel size, every panel in the plan is cut the same way; with several sizes, each panel may be cut differently. The search time is shared between the two directions. **Along the length**: rip the panel into long strips first, then cut the strips across — for saws or workflows that always rip first. **Across the length**: cut the panel across into shorter strips first. Parts with grain keep their direction whichever you choose. With unlimited stages, cuts may always go either way.
first_cuts.title: First cuts
first_cuts.x-short-help: Which way the first full-panel cuts run: either way, along or across the length.

kerf.description: The width of material each cut removes, in millimetres — the thickness of your saw blade's teeth, not the blade body. Every cut between two parts uses this much material, so parts are spaced by it. Typical values: 3.2–4.4 mm for panel and table saws, 2.2–2.8 mm for track saws. Leave it at 0 only if your dimensions already include it.
kerf.title: Saw blade thickness (kerf)
kerf.x-short-help: How much material each saw cut removes, in millimetres: usually 2.2–4.4 mm.

minimum_offcut_width.description: The narrowest offcut the plan may leave, in millimetres: thin offcuts can be thrown back by the blade or slip out of a panel saw's clamps. Every offcut, and the leftover, is at least this wide, measured across the cut that frees it; along that cut it may be as narrow as the parts beside it. Parts narrower than this are still cut. Along a trimmed edge, its *Trimmed strip* says whether the trim counts in the offcut's width. 0 allows any width, down to strips of saw dust; 20–50 mm is typical. A larger value can mean more waste.
minimum_offcut_width.title: Minimum offcut width
minimum_offcut_width.x-short-help: The narrowest offcut the plan may leave, so none is too thin to handle.

stages.description: How many times a piece is turned and cut again. **Stage 1**: full-length cuts across the whole panel, splitting it into strips. **Stage 2**: each strip is cut across into pieces. **Stage 3**: each piece is cut once more, across stage-2 cuts. More stages let parts nest more tightly, so less waste, but mean more handling at the saw. 2 suits simple strip cutting; 3 suits most panel-saw work; "Unlimited" gives the least waste with the most handling: cuts may then go either way at every stage, and the last-stage trimming setting does not apply.
stages.title: Cutting stages
stages.x-short-help: How often pieces are turned and cut again: more stages, less waste, more handling.

Solution.description: A cutting plan: one pattern per distinct way of cutting a panel.

patterns.description: The cutting patterns, in the order the panels are used.

Stages.description: The maximum number of cutting stages: 2, 3 or "unlimited".

StateEvent.description: The data of a `state` event: a job's state changed.

elapsed.description: Seconds spent searching so far, as in the job status.

ended_by.description: Why the job ended, as in the job status; `null` until it ends.

message.description: Why the job failed, in state `failed`; otherwise `null`.

plans_found.description: How many better plans have been found so far.

state.description: Where the job is in its life.

Trim.description: The strip cut off one edge of a panel.

cut.description: How the trimmed strip is cut away; it only matters with a *Minimum offcut width*. **Cut off first**: the strip is sawn off before any other cut, so the panel has a clean new edge and every offcut width is measured from it. **Left on the offcut**: the strip gets no cut of its own; it stays on the offcut along that edge and counts in its width, so fewer offcuts are too narrow. On the left end and the bottom edge, where cutting starts, such a strip is still cut away first, as an offcut at least *Minimum offcut width* wide, which can waste more. By default the left end and the bottom edge are cut off first and the right end and the top edge left on the offcut, which suits most jobs. With unlimited stages and no minimum offcut width, every strip is cut off first.
cut.title: Trimmed strip
cut.x-short-help: Whether the strip is sawn off first or stays on the offcut beside it.

width.description: How much to cut off this edge of the panel, in millimetres, to remove a chipped or damaged factory edge. No part is placed in it, and the saw cut that removes it is taken from it, so parts start exactly this far from the edge. Typical values: 5–15 mm on chipboard, MDF and melamine-faced board; more on a dented edge. Leave empty or 0 for a clean edge.
width.title: Trim
width.x-short-help: How much to cut off this edge to remove damage, in millimetres.

TrimCut.description: How a trimmed strip is cut away. See [`Trim::cut`].

Trims.description: The strips cut off a panel's four edges. An edge left out has no trim.

left.description: The left end, at the panel's origin (x = 0).

right.description: The right end, opposite the left one.

top.description: The top long edge, opposite the bottom one.

info.description: Cutting plans for sheet material: submit the parts, panels and saw settings, follow the search as it finds better plans, stop it when you like. See docs/API.md in the repository.

201.description: The job was created; usually `queued` or `running`.

delete.description: A queued job is cancelled at once; a running job stops at the solver's next check, normally within milliseconds. The response is the status at the time of the request, so it may still say `running`.

202.description: The stop was requested (or the job had already ended).
